questions.q: How does Naval apply compounding beyond money?
a: By building a reputation for reliability over time
By multiplying the number of jobs you hold
By treating friendships as financial assets
By saving time instead of spending it
questions.why: Lesson 1 says trust and referrals compound like invested returns.

questions.q: What is money's real purpose for Naval?
a: It buys freedom and time for what matters
It proves your value to other people
It removes the need for any work
It protects you from taking risks
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls money the ultimate tool for buying time.

questions.q: What does the tree metaphor teach about happiness?
a: Acknowledge each moment without judging it
Grow roots and stay in one place
Bend with the wind and avoid decisions
Compete for sunlight and never rest
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a tree is neutral, feeling what comes without labels.

questions.q: Why does the summary warn against upgrading your lifestyle?
a: Rising spending keeps you trapped on the treadmill
It makes friends resent your success
It attracts attention from tax authorities
It slows your investment returns
questions.why: Lesson 2 urges saving and investing instead of buying a bigger treadmill.

questions.q: What does Naval say about quieting the mind?
a: Sitting alone with your thoughts can bring peace
Silence should be avoided in favor of company
Meditation only works for experienced monks
Distraction is the fastest route to calm
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends facing thoughts and letting them go, as monks do.
